profile.headline: Principal Software Engineer at Wikimedia Foundation
profile.summary:
Web-based frontend and backend application developer for a variety of clients and audiences with extensive experience in early lifecycle development of products and companies.
 
 · Full time remote employee since 2013
 · Contributor to open source projects including MediaWiki and PECL.
 · Designed SDLC for PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance at a fast-growing private corporation.
 · Designed and led implementation of PCI-DSS and Sarbanes Oxley controls for a standalone division of a publicly traded company.
 · Designed and implemented Nation's first International Fuels Tax Agreement online electronic filing.
 · Designed and implemented Perl CGI based product catalog and shopping cart system which powered the first online grocery store in Austria.
 · Co-founder of web development and hosting company in 1996.

Specialties: Free and Open Source software development, business process automation, thinking like a bad guy while working for the good guys, getting products from idea to implementation

positions.description:
◆ Strategic and tactical planning in cooperation with Director of Technical Engagement
◆ Mentor and support engineers in Developer Advocacy and Cloud Services sub-teams
◆ Django/Python software development
◆ Product manager & lead developer for Toolhub (application catalog)

Role ended when the Technical Engagement group was dissolved by a reorganization of Wikimedia's engineering teams effective July 2023.

positions.title: Software Architect
positions.description:
Senior programmer and architect in team responsible for new product development.

 · Architect and developer for Kount® fraud control system.
 · Architect and primary developer for social networking reputation management product.
 · Architect and developer for DNS-based content filtering product.
 · Developer for credit card settlement and recurring billing system.

As an early hire into Keynetics' application development group I was a key contributor to many aspects of the software development process. I drafted our initial SDLC policies designed for PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance based on my prior experience with PCI-DSS and Sarbanes Oxley compliance and audits. I implemented our version control, continuous integration and build systems. I worked closely with the Operations group to ensure that deployment and maintenance of our software products met or exceeded their expectations.

I served as liaison between the R&D group and the development group for the productization of several business concepts. I was suited to this role due to strong technical and communication skills as well as a talent for communicating ideas clearly both "up" to management and "down" to technical staff.

Keynetics allowed me to contribute to several open source software projects that were aligned with the business goals and needs of the company. I contributed both bug fix and feature patches to established projects such as PHP, Phing and several other smaller projects. I adopted the abandoned php-yaml project, enhanced its functionality and got it admitted as an official PECL project. I also developed and published the iptools open source library available on PyPI for manipulating IP addresses to simplify the management of Django’s INTERNAL_IPS address list in a multi-developer environment.

Received Q3 2008 Keynetics Excellence Award for contribution to initial development of the Kount® fraud control system.

positions.title: Director of Development (Idaho)
positions.description:
Lead programmer and manager of technical group for eGovernment services company managing the official website for the State of Idaho.

As the DoD for the Idaho office of NIC I was responsible for all technical aspects of the Idaho portal including network infrastructure, application development, regulatory compliance and team management. At peak staffing I managed four developers, two graphic artists and a project manager either directly or indirectly. I interacted directly with clients from State offices, NIC management locally and at the corporate offices and peers in approximately 17 other NIC satellite offices.

Led design and development of Java-based application development library and framework that was used to implement over 50 eGovernment applications.

Architected and co-developed double-entry accounting application that handled all AccessIdaho credit card and recurring billing functions. Designed and implemented reports for accounting system that satisfied internal, central corporate and Sarbanes Oxley auditing requirements. Developed NACHA file interface that allowed daily ACH processing for distribution of collected funds to the State of Idaho within Constitutionally mandated 24 hour processing window.

Designed and implemented several applications for the Idaho Tax Commission including the first completely web-enabled International Fuels Tax Agreement (IFTA) filing and payment portal. The IFTA application won an award in the Taxation and Revenue category from the Center for Digital Government and Government Technology in November 2002.

I took an active role at the NIC corporate in technical groups including serving on the working group to standardize development practices across the enterprise and leading the Java practice group for several years. I was a strong champion for development of application frameworks to increase development velocity and gave several company wide presentations on the experiences we had in the Idaho office.

positions.title: Technical Director
positions.description:
Employee #2/co-founder of boutique Internet advertising/marketing agency.

Mediaphex was my version of graduate school. Bootstrapping an Internet presence that included commercial web and email hosting in 1996 wasn't the point and click activity that it is today. I installed, managed and in some cases built from mail-order parts: CSU/DSUs, routers, servers, desktops. When we got our first paying client I wrote sendmail.cf rules by hand to implement multi-tenant virtual hosts for email. As we grew I configured a Samba PDC for a LAN full of NT4 workstations. Then I had to figure out how to make it work with the OS9 Macs that we added.

We had a lot of great clients and cool projects. Clients ranged from a resort in Utah to hunting and rafting guides to a mail-order seed company to Hewlett-Packard and Extended Systems. We started with brochure-ware static sites but quickly progressed to database driven shopping sites, online sweepstakes fulfillment and what would eventually be called AJAX.

My favorite project was a series of 3 cd-roms which provided a simulation of HP's Web JetAdmin network printer monitoring and management software. I replicated the html interface from the actual product and paired it with a database and simulation engine written in javascript that would allow sales engineers to demo nearly all capabilities of the application from a laptop. The final installment of the project even used real MIB captures from HP's internal testing lab captured via a plugin I wrote for the real Web JetAdmin product.

Following my departure, Mediaphex merged with four other interactive agencies to form Wirestone in 2000. Wirestone was acquired by Accenture in 2017.

volunteerExperiences.description: Adopted an abandoned PECL extension for YAML parsing and emitting while working for Keynetics on the Kount project. Improved the project to support a wider range of YAML 1.1 constructs including merge key mappings and got the project accepted into the official pecl.php.net hosting environment.
